title: K-flat representative invariance of augmented scalar-extension Roos cones
statement:
Let $C$ be a site small in the module universe and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, with module category $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume countable products in $\mathcal A$ are exact. Let $B_{n+1}\to B_n$ for $n\ge1$ be a tower of sheaves of commutative $R$-algebras whose structure maps $R\to B_n$ commute with the transitions [def-weil-inverse-system]. No flatness or surjectivity of these ring maps is assumed. Use the unbounded derived category $D(R)$ and localization $Q$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], K-flat complexes with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For each such complex $P$, set $T_n(P)=P\otimes_RB_n$ with its strict transition maps, $V(P)=\prod_nT_n(P)$ termwise, and $s_P$ by $\operatorname{pr}_ns_P=t_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$. Define the Roos complex by
$$L(P)^i=V(P)^i\oplus V(P)^{i-1},\qquad d(x,y)=(dx,(1-s_P)x-dy),$$
and the chain map $\eta_P:P\to L(P)$ by $p\mapsto((p\otimes1)_n,0)$.
For a quasi-isomorphism $a:P\to P'$ between K-flat complexes with flat terms, the strict map $L(a)$ obtained by applying $\prod_n(a\otimes_RB_n)$ to both coordinates is a quasi-isomorphism and satisfies $L(a)\eta_P=\eta_{P'}a$. More generally, for every isomorphism $e:Q(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(P')$ in $D(R)$ there is an isomorphism $v:Q(L(P))\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(L(P'))$ satisfying $v\,Q(\eta_P)=Q(\eta_{P'})e$. Consequently the condition that $\eta_P$ be a quasi-isomorphism depends only on the derived isomorphism class of $P$.

proof.text: For each $n$, extension of scalars $E_n(M)=M\otimes_R B_n$ is additive: on a map $f$ it sends $m\otimes b$ to $f(m)\otimes b$, so it respects sums. Apply the ringed-site change-of-rings quasi-isomorphism lemma to $R\to B_n$ and the given map $a$ between K-flat complexes. It gives a quasi-isomorphism $a_n=a\otimes_R B_n:T_n(P)\to T_n(P')$. This remains a quasi-isomorphism after restricting scalars to $R$: kernels and cokernels in the two module-sheaf categories have the same underlying abelian sheaves, so their cohomology does too. No flatness of $B_n$ over $R$ is used. If $t_n,t'_n$ are the tower transitions, the identities $a_n t_n=t'_n a_{n+1}$ hold on $p\otimes b$ by the tensor formula. Thus $(a_n)_n$ is a strict tower map. The units $\gamma_n(p)=p\otimes1$ satisfy $t_n\gamma_{n+1}=\gamma_n$ because the algebra transitions preserve $1$. Consequently $(1-s_P)(\gamma_n)_n=0$, so the displayed $\eta_P$ is a chain map. Finally $a_n\gamma_n=\gamma'_n a$ in each coordinate, giving the strict equality $L(a)\eta_P=\eta_{P'}a$.

source.place: Tag 06YT, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side; Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change (change-of-rings case); coordinate naturality of sheaf tensor

proof.text: Regard $X(P)=(T_n(P))_n$ as a complex in $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$, with $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$. Kernels and cokernels in this abelian tower category are levelwise, so its cohomology is levelwise. Step 1 therefore makes $X(a)$ a quasi-isomorphism of tower complexes, and its image in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))$ is invertible. Apply the functor $\mathsf C$ of the strict Roos comparison, whose hypotheses are exactly the small-site and exact-countable-product hypotheses of the item. This sends that isomorphism to an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal A)$. With the cone convention of the derived-category definition, the signed interchange $(x,y)\mapsto(-y,x)$ identifies our $L(P)$ with $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_P)[-1]$; indeed the shifted-cone differential sends $(-y,x)$ to $(dy-(1-s_P)x,dx)$, which is the signed interchange of $d_{L(P)}(x,y)$. This identification commutes with the product maps on both coordinates. Hence the isomorphism just obtained is $Q(L(a))$. Since every cohomology functor factors through $Q$, invertibility of $Q(L(a))$ implies that every $H^i(L(a))$ is invertible. Thus $L(a)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: Let $e:Q(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(P')$ be the supplied derived isomorphism. Quasi-isomorphisms in $K(\mathcal A)$ admit a right calculus of fractions. The right-fraction representation lemma gives a complex $Z$ and homotopy-category maps $t:Z\to P$, $f:Z\to P'$ with $t$ a quasi-isomorphism and $e=Q(f)Q(t)^{-1}$. Choose chain-map representatives for $t,f$. The equation $Q(f)=eQ(t)$ makes $Q(f)$ invertible; applying the cohomology functors shows that $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The ringed-site K-flat resolution theorem gives $q:W\to Z$ a quasi-isomorphism with $W$ K-flat and termwise flat. Put $u=tq:W\to P$ and $b=fq:W\to P'$. Their cohomology maps are composites of isomorphisms, so both are quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes with flat terms. Moreover $Q(b)Q(u)^{-1}=Q(f)Q(q)(Q(t)Q(q))^{-1}=e$. Steps 1 and 2 apply to both $u$ and $b$. This constructs comparisons from a common representative, without asserting that a direct map $P\to P'$ exists.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution; derived.tex Tag 05RT, lemma-acyclic; categories.tex Tag 04VI, lemma-morphisms-right-localization, singleton case

proof.text:
Define $v=Q(L(b))Q(L(u))^{-1}$, which is an isomorphism by Step 2. Apply $Q$ to the two strict naturality equations from Step 1. The equation for $u$ gives $Q(L(u))^{-1}Q(\eta_P)=Q(\eta_W)Q(u)^{-1}$. Therefore
$$vQ(\eta_P)=Q(L(b))Q(\eta_W)Q(u)^{-1}=Q(\eta_{P'})Q(b)Q(u)^{-1}=Q(\eta_{P'})e.$$
Since $v$ and $e$ are invertible, this equation makes $Q(\eta_P)$ invertible if and only if $Q(\eta_{P'})$ is invertible. A chain map is a quasi-isomorphism if and only if its image under $Q$ is invertible: the forward direction is the localization property, and the reverse direction follows by applying every cohomology functor factoring through $Q$. This proves the final representative-invariance assertion.
